plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree producing fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before the leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and prized for ornamental and culinary use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in Japan as harbingers of spring, and the fruit is pickled into umeboshi or made into plum wine.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with drooping, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes through snow and carpets woodlands and gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (January to March)
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galantamine, a compound used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub covered in fluffy, fragrant golden flower balls. Its blooms are a vivid sight in woodlands and gardens near the end of the Southern Hemisphere summer and into autumn transitions in some areas.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in southeastern Australia, with some flowering extending from July to October
plants.location: Southeastern Australia (Victoria, South Australia, New South Wales)
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: A spectacular Himalayan tree bearing huge, goblet-shaped flowers on bare branches. Blooms can reach 25 cm across and are borne in great profusion on mature trees.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Himalayas (Nepal, Bhutan, northeast India, southwest China); cultivated in mild temperate gardens in the UK, New Zealand and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Trees may take 20 to 30 years from seed to flower for the first time, though grafted plants bloom much earlier.
